title: 5 Shillings - George VI (Festival of Britain)

obverse.description: Uncrowned portrait of King George VI left, legend above, denomination below.
obverse.lettering:
GEORGIVS VI D:G:BR:OMN:REX F:D:
HP
FIVE SHILLINGS
obverse.unabridged_legend:
Georgius VI Dei Gratia Britanniarum Omnium Rex Fidei Defensor
Humphrey Paget
obverse.lettering_translation: George the Sixth by the Grace of God King of all the Britains Defender of the Faith

reverse.description: St. George slaying the dragon right, date and designer's initials in exergue.

comments:
The standard weight of these coins was 10/11 troy ounce (436.4 grains). Under the Coinage Act of 1946, the composition changed from .500 silver to .750 copper/.250 nickel but the weight remained unchanged.

This coin was not included in demonetization legislation when decimalization was introduced in 1971. It has been confirmed by the Royal Mint that the coin remains legal tender, having been remonetized with a value of 25 pence.

edge.lettering: MDCCCLI CIVIUM INDUSTRIA FLORET CIVITAS MCMLI
edge.lettering_translation: 1851 By the industry of its people the state flourishes 1951
